frozen_hypothesis: A PO-01 defect can be converted into a frozen test and an isolated PO-03 repair candidate without ever touching a PO-01 namespace.
frozen_required_deliverable: A generator that emits a frozen failing test plus an integration-ready patch candidate held entirely inside the PO-03 namespace, with an assertion that no PO-01 path is written.
po01_contact_check: READ-ONLY CONFIRMED for everything this unit executes. Pack material is read via 'git cat-file' only, and the test materialises the pack tree into a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory created INSIDE the owned subtree - notably not under /tmp, which the commission forbids treating as durable. I attempted three separate escapes from the generator's output guard and all three were refused. See the caveat under HC-B about the emitted candidate, which is a shipped-artifact risk rather than an act this unit performed.

hidden_cases.rationale: The frozen deliverable's central safety property is that nothing escapes the PO-03 namespace. The producer asserts this but never attacks its own guard. I did, three ways.
hidden_cases.construction: Ran generate_candidate.py with --output-dir pointing at (1) an arbitrary scratch directory, (2) a directory whose name contains 'po01', and (3) a traversal into a SIBLING unit's subtree inside the same repository.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim:
HC-A arbitrary scratch dir              exit=1 refused=True msg=refusing output outside isolated candidate path: /home/ubuntu/po03-review-scratch-a/_hidden/023
HC-A path containing 'po01'             exit=1 refused=True msg=refusing output outside isolated candidate path: /home/ubuntu/po03-review-scratch-a/_hidden/023
HC-A traversal back to a sibling unit   exit=1 refused=True msg=refusing output outside isolated candidate path: /home/ubuntu/po03-review-scratch-a/_c3repo/wor
hidden_cases.interpretation: All three refused with exit 1 before any write. The guard is an equality test against a single resolved allowed path, which is the strongest form available and correctly also blocks writes into another unit's subtree - a prohibition the commission imposes independently.

hidden_cases.rationale: The generator guards itself, but the ARTIFACT it emits is a writer. The frozen deliverable calls it 'integration-ready', so whether the emitted candidate carries its own namespace guard is a real question nobody asked.
hidden_cases.construction: Materialised the pinned pack tree into a scratch directory deliberately NAMED '.../po01/packs' and ran the emitted repair_candidate.py against it. I never pointed it at any real packs/** path.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-B repair_candidate aimed at a path named .../po01/packs -> exit 0 | refused: False | written: ['06-browser-execution/_spine.py', '07-capability-manufacture/_spine.py', '08-knowledge-currentness/_spine.py', '09-infrastructure-operation/_spine.py', '10-economics-measurement/_spine.py']
hidden_cases.interpretation: The emitted repair candidate carries NO namespace guard at all. It writes into whatever --pack-root it is handed, including a path containing 'po01', with no refusal. The generator's careful guard protects only the generation step; the shipped artifact is an unguarded writer. This unit never applies it to PO-01 and its test applies it only to a temporary copy, so no prohibition was breached - but an 'integration-ready' patch candidate that will write anywhere is a live hazard for whoever picks it up next.

hidden_cases.rationale: Does the repair fail closed if a pack's declaration disagrees with the shared spine bytes? A repair that writes on mismatched declarations would corrupt rather than fix.
hidden_cases.construction: Copy of the pack tree with all _spine.py removed and 06-browser-execution's declared sha256 replaced by 64 zeros.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-C tampered declaration -> exit 1 | any _spine.py written: 0
hidden_cases.interpretation: Fails closed correctly: exit 1 and ZERO files written. The repair validates both the shared spine's own hash against a pinned constant and each pack's declaration against the observed bytes before writing anything.

hidden_cases.rationale: Idempotence probe. A repair that overwrites on re-run could silently clobber a differing file.
hidden_cases.construction: Ran the repair a second time on the already-repaired tree.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-D second repair run -> exit 0 | written: [] (empty = no overwrite)
hidden_cases.interpretation: Idempotent and non-destructive. The 'if not target.exists()' guard means it fills gaps and never overwrites existing bytes.

hidden_cases.rationale: Non-vacuity of the frozen test itself: it must actually fail before the repair, or the whole before/after demonstration is theatre.
hidden_cases.construction: Ran the emitted frozen_test_missing_spine.py against an unrepaired copy of the pack tree.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim: HC-E frozen test on unrepaired copy -> exit 1 | names 5 missing: 7
hidden_cases.interpretation: Genuinely fails with exit 1 and names the missing spine files in its assertion message. The frozen test is a real regression, not a placeholder.

hidden_cases.rationale: The repair hardcodes EXPECTED_SPINE_SHA256. If that constant were invented, the entire repair would be wrong while appearing to validate itself.
hidden_cases.construction: Independently hashed packs/_shared/_spine.py at the pinned commit and read the _spine.py declaration out of one of the five pack manifests.
hidden_cases.observed_output_verbatim:
packs/_shared/_spine.py PRESENT
431773539ced6556fdd9a631fc80d42404aa2f30846a1d127826dd099a01f182  -
  claimed EXPECTED_SPINE_SHA256 = 431773539ced6556fdd9a631fc80d42404aa2f30846a1d127826dd099a01f182
  06-browser-execution declares _spine.py sha256= 431773539ced6556fdd9a631fc80d42404aa2f30846a1d127826dd099a01f182 bytes= 43928
hidden_cases.interpretation: Three-way agreement confirmed by my own computation: the shared spine's actual bytes, the constant hardcoded in the repair candidate, and the declaration inside the pack manifest all give SHA-256 431773539ced... at 43928 bytes. The repair restores the correct bytes and the constant is a real measurement.

producer_declared_limitations: The repair is an unpromoted candidate held under PO-03; it was never applied to a published pack, PO-01 namespace, branch, path, PR, artifact or workspace.
scope_honesty_assessment.assessment: Exactly the right limitation, enumerated rather than gestured at, and I could not falsify any part of it. The defect.json artifact independently records po01_path_writes as an empty list and candidate_scope as 'held entirely under this PO-03 unit; never applied to PO-01'. What is undeclared is that the emitted candidate has no guard of its own (HC-B), which matters precisely because the deliverable advertises it as integration-ready.

reproducibility_check: Commit-pinned. The generate/fail/repair/pass cycle reproduced identically in fresh python3 -I processes, and the repair proved idempotent on a second application.
disposition_reason: The PASS is justified and this is the best-engineered unit in cohort c3. Every element of the frozen deliverable is present and I verified each independently: the frozen test genuinely fails on an unrepaired tree, the repair candidate genuinely fixes it on an isolated copy, the whole thing is held inside the PO-03 namespace, and the no-PO-01-write assertion survived three separate escape attempts including a traversal into a sibling unit's subtree. The repair is also safer than it needed to be - it validates the shared spine against a pinned hash and each pack's declaration before writing, fails closed with zero writes on a tampered declaration, and is idempotent rather than overwriting. I confirmed the hardcoded spine hash three ways against the real bytes and the real manifest declaration, so nothing is invented. The unit converts the five-absent-_spine.py defect that units 020 and 022 refuted into an executable regression instead of a narrative, which is what the commission asks for. One hazard is logged rather than held against it: the emitted candidate itself has no namespace guard.
followups_for_coordinator: The emitted repair_candidate.py has no namespace guard of its own. Reviewer-observed: aimed at a scratch tree named '.../po01/packs' it wrote all five _spine.py files with no refusal and exit 0. Since the frozen deliverable advertises this artifact as integration-ready, the generator should emit it with the same path assertion it applies to itself, so the guard travels with the candidate rather than staying behind in the generator.

Positive note worth propagating to other units: this unit's test creates its temporary pack copy with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) rather than under /tmp, which respects the commission's prohibition on treating /tmp as durable evidence. Several other units in the wave use /tmp-backed TMPDIR indirection instead.
